Bayesian calibration of the clumped isotope paleothermometer

Source: R/cal.bayesian.R
cal.bayesian.Rd

Fits up to three Bayesian linear regressions of D47 on temperature using Stan.

Usage

cal.bayesian(
  calibrationData,
  models = c("errors", "noerrors", "mixed"),
  priors = "Informative",
  numSavedSteps = 3000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = getOption("mc.cores", 1L),
  MC = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'bayclump_cal'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

Arguments

calibrationData

The calibration dataset. It needs the columns Temperature (10^6/T^2, with T in K), TempError (1 SD of Temperature), D47, and D47error (1 SD of D47). The mixed model also needs Material.

models

The models to fit. Use any of "errors", "noerrors", and "mixed".

priors

Priors on the intercept (alpha) and slope (beta). Use "Informative", "Weak", or "Flat", or a list such as list(alpha = c(0.231, 0.065), beta = c(0.039, 0.004)) with the mean and SD of each normal prior. "Uninformative" is kept as another name for "Flat".

numSavedSteps

Total number of posterior draws to keep across all chains.

chains

Number of MCMC chains.

cores

Number of cores used to run the chains in parallel.

MC

Deprecated. Use cores instead.

x

A bayclump_cal object.

digits

Number of decimal places to print.

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class bayclump_cal. It is a list of stanfit objects named BLM1_fit, BLM1_fit_NoErrors, and BLM3_fit, with the priors and a convergence summary stored as attributes. Use cal.draws() to get the posterior draws and cal.compare() to compare models.

Details

The three models are:

  • "errors" (BLM1_fit) accounts for errors in both Temperature and D47. Its sigma is the scatter left after removing the measurement error in D47. The true temperatures have a normal prior with a mean and SD estimated from the data.

  • "noerrors" (BLM1_fit_NoErrors) ignores both errors, so its sigma includes the measurement error.

  • "mixed" (BLM3_fit) lets intercepts and slopes vary by Material around shared means (partial pooling). It ignores measurement errors. The priors apply to the shared means. The SDs among materials have half-normal priors with scales of 0.1 (intercepts) and 0.01 (slopes). With fewer than five materials, these SDs are mostly set by their priors. The model is skipped when there are fewer than two materials.

The "Informative" values are the ones used in earlier versions of this package. Check that they suit the reference frame of your data, or set your own.

A warning is given when a model shows signs of poor convergence: Rhat above 1.01, fewer than 100 effective draws per chain, or divergent transitions.
